details: On June 20, 2026, Iran's military announced it had closed the Strait of Hormuz, a crucial global oil shipping route. This action was reportedly in response to alleged breaches of a ceasefire agreement by the United States and ongoing Israeli military operations in Lebanon. However, the United States swiftly denied the closure, with Vice President J.D. Vance asserting that the Strait remains open and commercial shipping traffic continues unimpeded. U.S. Central Command further stated that 55 merchant ships, carrying over 17 million barrels of oil, transited the Strait on June 20. This escalating tension occurs as U.S. and Iranian officials are scheduled to resume high-level peace talks in Switzerland on June 21 to discuss the fragile ceasefire agreement.
title: Iran Claims Hormuz Closure Amid US Denial, Peace Talks Continue

details: The U.S. House Oversight Subcommittee on Military and Foreign Affairs is slated to host a roundtable on June 25, 2026. Titled "Two Sides of a Digital Coin: Protecting U.S. Security by Challenging the Power of Repressive Foreign Regimes," the session will examine how digital assets and cryptocurrencies can empower individuals in nations experiencing economic instability or authoritarian rule. The discussion will also delve into how U.S. leadership in digital finance can affect national security interests and global economic competitiveness.
title: US Congress to Probe Crypto's Role in National Security and Economic Sovereignty
